newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Formosa up on Australia project report.
newsitem.headline: Formosa up on Australia project report.

text.p: Taiwan's Formosa Plastics group shares surged at mid-morning on Monday on a local newspaper report that the group may build a petrochemical complex in Australia, brokers said.

Formosa, Taiwan's biggest industrial conglomerate, began considering the project after its chairman visited Queensland in 1996 to seek coal imports for his company's petrochemical complex in southern Taiwan, the Economic Daily News reported.
After 80 minutes, Formosa Plastics surged T$3.5 or 5.15 percent to T$71.5 and Nan Ya Plastics was up T$3.5 or 4.97 percent to T$74.
Both shares are key members of the Formosa group.
The newspaper said the Australian complex would export petrochemical products to other Asian countries, including China.
Formosa officials declined to comment on the report.
"Formosa Plastics group shares have lagged behind this year's gains, so bargain hunters are buying them," said Michael Hung, an independent senior analyst.
"The reported Australia project simply gives investors an excuse to buy the shares, although everyone knows the report is pretty vague," Hung said. -- Taipei newsroom (5080815)
